lens: The paradoxical role of senolytics in bone marrow adiposity (BMAT) expansion and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) reveals a tissue-specific efficacy trade-off, where senescent cell clearance may inadvertently promote lipogenesis in irradiated bone while destabilizing vascular plaques in atherosclerosis models.
known_to_ignore: Aging is associated with senescent cell accumulation
SASP factors contribute to tissue dysfunction
tensions: ABT-263 at 100 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg reduced smooth muscle cells by 90% but caused >50% mortality in advanced atherosclerotic Apoe-/- mice (JCI Insight 2024)
D+Q treatment decreased miR34a (P = 0.016) yet increased p53 gene expression (P = 0.041) in aging mice (Aging 2020)
BMAT was upregulated at day 7 post-radiation, but senolytic D+Q effects were observed at day 42, suggesting timing-dependent interactions (Journal of Bone and Mineral Research 2020)
gaps: The dose-response relationship of ABT-263 on EndoMT across different atherosclerosis stages
The impact of senolytics on BMAT in human subjects aged >70 years with senescent cell prevalence >50%
The role of irisin as a mediator between senolytic therapy and bone mineral density in clinical populations

theses.title: Senolytic-Induced EndoMT as a Hidden Risk Factor in Atherosclerotic Plaque Destabilization
theses.rationale: Drawing from JCI Insight 2024 data on ABT-263 increasing EndoMT by 60% in Apoe-/- mice, this angle challenges the assumption that senolytics uniformly improve vascular health and could inform targeted drug design to avoid off-target effects.

theses.title: miR-27a Modulation and BMAT Dynamics: A Mechanistic Link Between Radiation-Induced Senescence and Bone Loss
theses.rationale: Integrating findings from Journal of Bone and Mineral Research 2020 on miR-27a downregulation by D+Q and BMAT upregulation in radiated C57BL/6 mice, this review proposes a pathway where senolytics may mitigate bone loss by targeting senescence-driven adipogenesis.

reviewer_objections: The high mortality rate (>50%) in ABT-263-treated Apoe-/- mice may stem from model-specific factors like western diet or genetic background, limiting translational relevance to human senolytic trials
The correlation between irisin serum levels and femoral BMD (R = 0.619) in older adults is observational and does not demonstrate causality for senolytic interventions
Evidence strength for senolytic effects on BMAT is limited to a single murine study at 42 days post-radiation, requiring longer-term and multi-model validation
next_extractions: Dose-titration studies of ABT-263 in early versus advanced atherosclerosis models to assess EndoMT thresholds
Temporal analysis of BMAT changes in human bone biopsies following senolytic therapy for osteoporosis
Clinical measurement of irisin levels in senolytic trials to evaluate its potential as a biomarker for bone health outcomes
